situation: The Guest search, for a Staff Member of two Organizations
given: a Staff Member belongs to two Organizations, so guests_read_own_organization admits the Guests of both
when: they search for a Guest while working in one of them
then: deferred: there is no Guest search on main. The decision recorded for it (AGENTS.md 'Testing security claims', PR #43) is that the search filters on organization_id AND runs under guests_read_own_organization; the policy alone admits both Organizations and only the filter picks one, so that divergence is the assertion. The search and its test live on the unmerged feat/guest-profile line of work (PR #43, #45). On main the only search is the client-side filter of the Reservations list (guest name, Unit, room, reference) over one Property's rows.

given: a Staff Member holding front_desk.book at a Property with the front desk capability, a sellable Unit in service, and at least one night from the Property's today
then: the Guest is identified or recorded, the Reservation is written confirmed (not requested, because a front desk taking a booking is allocating the Unit — ADR 0024), and reservation.created is recorded in the audit log inside the same transaction with the Guest's id (ADR 0012: the audit record is inside a multi-write command)
test_name: front-office.test.ts: records the Guest and the Reservation, and shows them on the list

situation: An enquiry is not an allocation
given: a requested Reservation over nights another Reservation on the same Unit also covers
then: accepted: reservations_no_double_booking holds confirmed Reservations only, and refusing a second enquiry would be an availability policy nobody has specified (ADR 0024). Nothing in the product writes requested yet (RG-DEF-03).
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a requested Reservation holds nothing

given: a confirmed Reservation holds a Unit for some nights
when: a second confirmed Reservation is taken over any of those nights
then: refused by the exclusion constraint (23P01), which the module reports as UnitUnavailableError and the form as 'That Unit is already booked for those nights'. Availability is a constraint, never a query (ADR 0024, ADR 0012).
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a second confirmed Reservation cannot overlap on one Unit

situation: CONCURRENCY — two clerks book one Unit at once
given: two connections take a booking for the same Unit and overlapping nights at the same moment, for two different Guests
then: exactly one Reservation exists; the loser fails on the constraint rather than on an application check, and the Guest the loser described is not on file because the whole booking is one transaction (ADR 0024, ADR 0012)
test_name: front-office.test.ts: produces exactly one Reservation, and the loser fails on the constraint

given: a confirmed Reservation ends on the 4th
when: another is taken on the same Unit starting on the 4th
then: accepted: nights are half-open, daterange(starts_on, ends_on, '[)'), the same shape as stays_no_double_booking (ADR 0024)
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: somebody may arrive on the day the last Guest leaves

given: a booking whose departure is the same day as its arrival, or earlier
then: refused: ReservationPeriodError from the module, and reservations_period_check (ends_on > starts_on, 23514) for every role, because an empty daterange overlaps nothing and would hold no Unit (ADR 0024)
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a Reservation covers at least one night

given: an arrival date before the Property's own today (app.property_today, not the server's clock)
then: refused with ReservationPeriodError 'a Reservation cannot start before today'. The code and a test do this, but no ADR or PR states it as a decision, and nothing in the database refuses it — a caller outside the module can write one.
test_name: front-office.test.ts: refuses dates that are not a period a Reservation can have

situation: A date that does not exist
given: an arrival of 2027-02-31, which matches the pattern and a lenient parser reads as 3 March
then: refused with ReservationPeriodError before any transaction opens; the form reports the period as invalid. Code and test only, no stated decision.
test_name: front-office.test.ts: refuses dates that are not a period a Reservation can have

given: 01:30 at a Property whose business-day cutoff is 04:00, so its today is still yesterday's date (ADR 0021)
when: a booking is taken for yesterday's calendar date
then: accepted: the past-date check compares with app.property_today, and ADR 0021 says every date comparison became a business-date comparison. Follows from the code; no test books across the cutoff.

given: no departure date is given
when: a booking is taken, for either stay type
then: accepted with ends_on null; it holds the Unit from its arrival onwards (the constraint's daterange is unbounded). Nothing ties an open-ended booking to the resident stay type — a short-term Guest can be booked with no end. The sources neither allow nor forbid that.
test_name: front-office.test.ts: books the same person again rather than opening a second record

situation: A checked-in Reservation leaves the constraint
given: a confirmed Reservation is checked in
when: another confirmed booking is taken over its nights
then: the Reservation constraint no longer counts it — its Stay holds the Unit instead, which is what lets a room be re-let the morning its Guest leaves; the in-house Stay then refuses the booking through the ADR 0033 trigger (FD-S2-03). Stated by PR #41, commit 949b667 and ADR 0033. SOURCE CONFLICT: ADR 0024's Decision section shows the constraint as status in ('confirmed', 'checked_in') and says checked_in is an allocation, while the migration, the PR, ADR 0033 and this test say confirmed alone. ADR 0024 now carries an Amended: line saying so: the constraint shipped as confirmed alone in 949b667, the commit that implemented it.
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: the double-booking constraint is partial on confirmed alone

given: the Organization already has a Guest at nezihe@example.test, recorded as 'Nezihe Muhiddin'
when: somebody books 'N. Muhiddin' at the same address
then: the existing Guest is reused (guestCreated false), both Reservations name them, and the profile keeps its own name: a second booking is not an edit (ADR 0024). The insert is on conflict ... do update set updated_at = updated_at, a no-op that makes RETURNING give back the existing row.
test_name: front-office.test.ts: books the same person again rather than opening a second record

given: a Guest is on file at ada@example.test
then: the address is trimmed and lowercased before the insert and guests_email_is_normalized refuses anything stored otherwise, so the unique index matches the existing Guest. ADR 0024 says 'exact email'; that case and whitespace are folded first is stated only in the migration's comment.
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: an address is stored normalized, so two spellings cannot become two people

given: two people are booked, neither with an email
then: two Guests: nothing distinguishes them and guessing would be the automatic merge blueprint 18.7 forbids. The unique index is partial on email being present (ADR 0024). The same applies to every Guest backfilled from reservations.guest_name.
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a second Guest with no email is a second person

situation: The Guest's Stay summary checks its caller
given: app.guest_stay_summary() is a security definer that checks the caller's Organization and the capability
then: deferred: the function is not on main. The decision recorded for it (AGENTS.md 'Testing security claims'): the capability is asked about the Guest's Organization, and reaching a Property there requires membership there, so the capability implies the Organization check and deleting that clause failed nothing. The two never diverge, so the clause is untested and stays only because a future change to the shared helper would widen the function silently. It lives on the unmerged feat/guest-profile line of work (PR #43).

situation: A similar name, or a shared telephone
given: a Guest is on file as 'Ada Lovelace' with +90 212 000 00 00
when: a booking gives the same name or the same telephone and no email, or another email
then: a second Guest. Matching is an exact email within the Organization and nothing else; a name, a telephone or a date of birth belongs to staff duplicate review (ADR 0024, blueprint 18.7). Stated, but no test books a name or telephone collision and asserts two records.

given: Organization B has a Guest at grace@example.test
when: Organization A books somebody at grace@example.test
then: a separate Guest in Organization A. The index is (organization_id, email) and the Organization comes from the Unit's row, never from the caller. ADR 0024 says 'within the Organization'; no test books one address in two Organizations.

situation: CONCURRENCY — one returning Guest booked twice at once
given: two clerks book the same new address for different Units at the same moment
then: one Guest and two Reservations: on conflict leaves no window between a lookup and an insert, where a select-then-insert would let one clerk hit the unique index. Stated in identifyGuestWithin's comment; not tested.

situation: The Guest grants are asserted column by column
given: public.guests' INSERT grant was table-level (20260916002000), so a new column becomes insertable
then: owned by IG-15, whose exact-set assertion goes red on the count of insertable columns. This id is kept because insert-grants/design.md:18 cites it: on feat/guest-profile it asserted the INSERT set and caught status and merged_into_id becoming insertable

situation: A refused booking leaves no Guest
given: a booking is refused — the Unit is out of reach, or the constraint refuses it
then: no Guest is left behind: the Unit is read before the Guest is recorded, and the Guest, the Reservation, the event and the audit record are one transaction (ADR 0012)
test_name: front-office.test.ts: refuses a Unit in a Property the viewer cannot reach

situation: A Guest belongs to the Organization
given: a Staff Member assigned to one of an Organization's two Properties
then: they read every Guest of the Organization, including people who never stayed at their Property: a Guest is not Property-scoped, and a front desk that could not find them would create a duplicate. Deliberately the widest read in the product; Stays, Folios and rates stay Property-scoped (ADR 0024).
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a Staff Member assigned to one Property reaches the Organization's Guests

given: a Staff Member of Organization A
then: none of Organization B's come back (blueprint 7.1, ADR 0024)
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a Staff Member reads their own Organization's Guests and no others

situation: Recording a Guest for another Organization
given: a Staff Member of Organization A, and a row naming Organization B, which exists and is active
then: refused (42501) by guests_insert_front_desk: the four gates are asked of the Organization the row names, and they reach no Property of it (ADR 0024)
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a Guest cannot be recorded for another Organization

situation: A Reservation naming another Organization's Guest
given: a Reservation in Organization A with the id of a Guest in Organization B
then: refused (23503) by the composite foreign key (guest_id, organization_id): unrepresentable rather than refused by a policy somebody could widen (ADR 0012, values come from rows and composite keys prove them)
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a Reservation cannot name another Organization's Guest

given: a Staff Member of one Organization names a Unit at another Organization's Property
then: refused with ReservationRefusedError, the same answer as a Unit that does not exist, and nothing is written; underneath, reservations_insert_front_desk and the composite foreign keys refuse the row for every role (ADR 0012)
test_name: front-office.test.ts: refuses a Unit in a Property the viewer cannot reach

situation: Booking at an unassigned Property of one's own Organization
given: a Staff Member with assigned_properties reach, assigned to Property A only
when: they take a booking on a Unit at Property B of the same Organization
then: refused with ReservationRefusedError: gate 4 (reach) is in both the Unit read and the insert policy. Follows from the policy; no test books at an unassigned Property of the same Organization. The Guest read stays Organization-wide (RG-S1-23).

given: a booking names Property A and a Unit that belongs to Property B
then: refused by the composite foreign key (accommodation_unit_id, property_id, organization_id) for every role; the module's Unit read also returns nothing (ADR 0012)
test_name: reservations_and_check_in.test.sql: a Unit from another Property cannot be reserved

situation: A lapsed Organization records no Guest
given: the Subscription is suspended, or the front_office Entitlement is revoked, or no Property has the front desk, or the actor reaches none
then: refused by each gate on its own: app.can_use_capability_in_organization() asks blueprint 3.5's four gates of any one Property of the Organization the actor reaches, so a lapsed Subscription stops Guests being recorded and not merely listed (ADR 0024)
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: gate 1 denies the write: a suspended Subscription records nothing

situation: A lapsed Organization takes no booking
given: the Subscription is suspended, or the Property has no front desk
then: refused by reservations_insert_front_desk, which carries the commercial gates because a write has no query around it to carry them (ADR 0012)
test_name: reservations_and_check_in.test.sql: gate 1 denies the write: a suspended Subscription creates nothing

situation: Losing the front desk does not hide people
given: the Organization's only front-desk Property has the capability switched off
when: a Staff Member reads Guests directly
then: the Organization's existing Guests still come back: guests_read_own_organization is reach alone, and the gates stop recording, not reading. Every screen that shows a Guest reads through a query that carries the gates itself (listReservations). Stated only in the test's comment.
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a Property without a front desk still reads the Organization's Guests

situation: A role without front_desk.book records a Guest
given: a Staff Member whose role lacks front_desk.book, with every gate open
then: refused: guests_insert_front_desk carries front_desk.book as a fifth conjunct (ADR 0026, migration 20260916002300). The Reservation half is asserted by SP-S2-02 ('and the fifth refuses anyway: taking a booking is not their job'); nothing asserts the Guest half on its own.

given: a Resident with a current Stay signed in to the Portal
when: they read Guests or record one
then: they read none and record none: guests_read_own_organization resolves through app.accessible_organization_ids(), which needs a membership a Resident never has (ADR 0009, ADR 0024)
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a Resident reaches no Guest at all

given: a Resident with a current Stay at a Property
when: they insert a Reservation, even at their own Property
then: refused, and they read no Reservation (ADR 0009)
test_name: reservations_and_check_in.test.sql: a Resident cannot create a Reservation, not even in their own Property

given: the runtime role with no acting user set
when: a Guest is read or recorded
then: nothing is readable and the insert is refused: the policies see a null acting user and deny (ADR 0007)
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: without a request context no Guest can be recorded

situation: A room let by the bed
given: a room with beds under it
then: refused for every role by the sellability trigger, and the room is not offered on the booking form; each bed inside it can be booked (ADR 0025)
test_name: unit_hierarchy.test.sql: a room that is let by the bed cannot be booked as a whole

given: a room with a confirmed booking on it
when: somebody adds a bed under it
then: refused while a current Stay or Reservation names it; once the booking is cancelled the room may be divided (ADR 0025)
test_name: unit_hierarchy.test.sql: a room somebody has booked cannot be divided underneath them

given: a booking is taken
when: reservation.created is written to the outbox
then: the payload carries ids only — Reservation, Guest, Property, Unit — and no name or contact detail, as ADR 0017 requires of every payload; nothing subscribes to it yet. No test asserts this event's payload (the check-in event has one).

given: a booking
then: stay_type is guest or resident (reservations_stay_type_check); the form offers both and defaults to guest; anything else is refused by the server action before the module. Code only, no test.

given: a name, an optional email and an optional telephone
then: the name is trimmed and 1 to 120 characters, the email at most 254 and the telephone at most 40; an empty email or telephone becomes absent. The check constraints are the boundary; GUEST_DETAILS publishes their bounds so the form's maxLength cannot drift. A refusal is GuestDetailsError, which the form shows as one generic message rather than by field.
test_name: new-reservation.test.tsx: stops at the lengths the Guest table will accept

situation: An email shorter than three characters
given: guests_email_is_normalized requires 3 to 254 characters, and GUEST_DETAILS publishes a maximum only
when: a caller outside the browser form submits a one- or two-character email
then: the module passes it, the database refuses it with 23514, which createReservation does not map, so the desk sees 'That booking cannot be taken' and it is logged as unexpected. The browser's type=email makes it hard to reach from the form. Whether GUEST_DETAILS should publish the minimum is unanswered.

situation: Amending a booking through the grant
given: a role that may update a Reservation — check-in, check-out or cancel
when: it rewrites the Reservation's dates or Unit
then: refused: ranza_app may update only a Reservation's status and timestamp. A policy bounds rows and a grant bounds columns (ADR 0012, amended 2026-09-16), so amending and room moves are a deliberate widening, not a side effect (docs/roadmap.md)
test_name: reservations_and_check_in.test.sql: a Reservation's dates cannot be rewritten by whoever may check it in

given: any Reservation
then: refused: no DELETE policy and no grant; a booking ends as cancelled or no_show and keeps its dates (blueprint 7.4, ADR 0012)
test_name: reservations_and_check_in.test.sql: a Reservation is never deleted, it is cancelled

situation: Editing a Guest through the runtime role
given: a Guest on file, and a Staff Member whom guests_update_front_desk admits
when: they change the Guest's name or email
then: refused (42501): the policy permits the row and the column grant is the only thing that refuses it. ranza_app holds UPDATE on updated_at alone, which exists for the no-op conflict update; nothing edits a Guest until a screen that says so widens the grant deliberately (ADR 0024). On feat/guest-profile the same row forbade UPDATE of the merge's status and merged_into_id (docs/features/insert-grants/design.md).
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a Guest's name cannot be edited through the runtime role; guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: the runtime role may update exactly one column of a Guest

given: a Guest on file
then: refused: no DELETE policy and no grant. A person is not removed from the record; blueprint 18.7 and 7.5 ask for anonymization under a retention policy, which is a workflow (RG-DEF-08), and history is not silently removed (blueprint 7.4)
test_name: guests_and_reservation_creation.test.sql: a Guest is never deleted

given: a confirmed booking whose nights have all passed with nobody arriving
when: the Reservations list is read the next morning
then: it is still listed, and can be marked a no-show there: a booking still requested or confirmed stays however old it is, because it is on no other screen (PR #60, finding 10)
test_name: front-office.test.ts: stays on the Reservations list after its nights pass, and can be marked a no-show there

given: a Property's Reservations in every status
then: every Reservation whose last night has not passed, whatever became of it — cancelled, no-show, checked out — because a booking that vanished when cancelled would read as one never taken; plus RG-S3-01. Each row carries the Guest's name and email, the stay type, the dates, the Unit and whether the viewer may cancel or mark a no-show. Stated in the module's comment; no test lists a cancelled booking.

given: a Property with no Reservation from today onwards
then: an empty state: 'Nothing booked ahead — Nothing is booked at this Property from today onwards.' No test renders it.

given: a Property whose Units are all blocked, out of service, or rooms let by the bed with no free leaf
then: the New reservation button is not offered, because the form would have nothing to choose. No test.

situation: A viewer who may not book
given: a Staff Member whose role lacks front_desk.book, at a Property with Units in service
then: the New reservation button is offered anyway and the booking is refused on submit as 'That booking cannot be taken'. The page's comment says hiding it would be a second, weaker copy of the policy; PR #60 (finding 11) says controls a role cannot use are not shown, and FD-S5-03 applies that to check-in, undo, check-out, cancel and no-show but not to booking. Which one holds for booking is unanswered.

situation: A Property this screen is not for
given: a ?property= naming a Property without the front desk, one the viewer cannot use, or a forged id
then: the no-front-desk empty state, never another Property's bookings (PR #63)
test_name: front-desk-property.test.ts: shows nothing, not another Property, for one where this screen is switched off

situation: Two different refusals the desk can act on
given: the nights are held by another confirmed booking, or by somebody in house
then: two different refusals, which the screen words differently: 'That Unit is already booked for those nights' (23P01, solved by moving a booking) and 'Somebody is staying in that Unit for some of those nights' (55006, solved by checking somebody out), because the desk solves them differently (ADR 0033). Only the module's UnitHasOccupantError is asserted; the two messages themselves are not
test_name: front-office.test.ts: refuses a booking over nights somebody in house is staying for

situation: Every other refusal is one answer
given: the Unit is out of reach, unentitled, out of service, let by the bed, in another Property, or does not exist
then: one message, 'That booking cannot be taken', for all six: telling them apart would confirm that a Unit the caller cannot see exists. Stated in the module's comment; the test covers the out-of-reach case.
test_name: front-office.test.ts: refuses a Unit in a Property the viewer cannot reach

given: the database is unreachable, or a refusal the action does not name
then: the desk sees 'That booking cannot be taken' and the error is logged server-side as unexpected, never swallowed. Code only, no test.

given: the form is submitted and the booking is taken
then: it closes by the booking having happened, the list gains the row, and the row shows the Guest's email as the visible evidence that a returning Guest would be recognized. Asserted in the browser; stated only in the component's comments.
test_name: reservations.spec.ts: a front desk takes a booking and finds it on the list

given: the booking form
then: arrival and departure are native date inputs submitting YYYY-MM-DD, arrival required and departure optional with the hint 'Leave empty for an open-ended Reservation'. Open PR #71 replaces them with one DateRangeField submitting the same names.
test_name: new-reservation.test.tsx: asks for dates the module can read

given: the booking form, its refusals and the list
when: they are read in tr, en or ar
then: every string comes from the typed catalogue, so a key missing in one language fails the typecheck (ADR 0023); Arabic mirrors through logical utilities. No test renders the booking form in Arabic.

situation: Amending a booking's dates or Unit
given: a confirmed booking whose dates change, or whose Unit is blocked
when: the desk wants to amend it
then: deferred: docs/roadmap.md names 'amending a booking and moving a Guest' as next slice 2; until then a booking is cancelled and taken again, and RG-S1-43 refuses the columns

situation: Moving an in-house Guest to another Unit
given: a Guest in house
then: deferred: transfers are the one unbuilt item in the roadmap's Reservations row and are refused by a column-level grant; PR #60 lists moving a Guest as not built

given: a requested Reservation written by a booking engine or a channel
then: deferred: nothing writes requested yet. ADR 0024 says confirming will be the act that has to pass reservations_no_double_booking

given: any of them
then: deferred: blueprint 5.3 lists them, and the reservations migration (…000900) gives them no status because inventing one would invent the workflow (blueprint section 13)

situation: Duplicate review and merging two Guests
given: two records that may be one person
then: deferred: blueprint 18.7 asks for staff to review the evidence, choose the survivor, preview the impact and produce an audit record, never an automatic merge. ADR 0024 keeps it out of the booking form; the merge lives on the unmerged feat/guest-profile line of work

given: a Guest's name, email or telephone is wrong
then: deferred: an edit 'belongs to a screen that says so' (ADR 0024) and must widen the update grant deliberately; nothing edits a Guest today (RG-S2-25)

situation: Documents, guardians, emergency contacts, preferences, consent
given: a Guest
then: deferred: all blueprint 18.7, not built (docs/roadmap.md, 'Guest and Resident profiles' row; packages/ranza/guests README)

given: a Guest under a retention policy
then: deferred: anonymization under a retention policy is the workflow blueprint 18.7 and 7.5 ask for, instead of a DELETE (migration 20260916002000)

given: a Guest's history across Reservations and Stays
then: deferred: blueprint 18.7, 'partial' in the roadmap. When built it brings its own capability key and guests_insert_front_desk gains an OR clause, not a replacement, so the front desk keeps working without it (ADR 0024)

given: a desk wants a timeline, a conflict preview, a side drawer or alternative dates when a Unit is taken
then: deferred: blueprint 18.6; the roadmap says the timeline is not built and the list stays a list until a Unit has a floor and a rate

given: a booking
then: deferred: nothing has a price; a rate is next slice 1 in docs/roadmap.md
